entityDescription:
Computer vision (CV) is a discipline that focuses on developing techniques through which computers can perceive and interpret the content of digital images. CV is used in many industrial applications for quality control or anomaly detection, and increasingly, CV systems are based on artificial intelligence (AI) for image analysis. In AI developments, data is the most crucial and valuable pillar. In the real world, collecting accurate and high-quality data is complex, expensive, and time-consuming. A certain portion of the labelled data will contain inaccuracies due to human interaction in the annotation process. Additionally, for rare defects / anomalies, the difficulty of collecting a sufficient number of images is even greater, especially in space applications where products or applications are produced in very small batches. 
With our product, Synigen, the customer can generate accurate, high-quality, automatically annotated, and labelled realistic synthetic images of a 3D object or scene with the automatic integration of anomalies or defects on the chosen objects. The intuitive graphical interface allows the user to create large datasets of a product containing defects/anomalies even before the actual production begins. This dataset can be used as input for training an AI model that can be used in any computer vision task. The advantages compared to real data are: 
- Speed: there is no need to wait for the "real-world" setup to capture a sufficient number of images suitable for anomaly detection, even for rarely occurring anomalies. 
- Accuracy: our images are automatically labeled and annotated, eliminating biases/errors introduced by human interaction in the process. 
- Flexibility: the models can be easily updated or modified without costly impact. 
- Cost: compared to "real-world" images, our synthetic images cost only a fraction.
With our approach, non-software people can create the necessary data, leaving the software/machine learning engineers use their skills and talent to other complicated tasks. 
A CV based on our solution would be a perfect add-on for: 
• automated anomaly inspection (defects, wrong assembly, PCB…) or for self-diagnostics of systems 
• automated object recognition for spatial situational awareness (debris or adversarial entities) or for part detection 
 
Besides the software, our company is specialized in the development of the needed hardware, with or without robots, for capturing the needed anomalies in an image as well as doing inference on these images allowing self-diagnostics or situational awareness.
The existing NDT (non-destructive testing) for major aerospace suppliers (materials, engine parts, bolts…) can benefit of our solution. In a further future, automatically conditioned and functioning farms and systems will be necessary in long distance travelling (to Mars) or missions on the surface of Mars / Moon. Therefore, an AI system helping the detection of anomalies will be inevitable.

Founded by a world-leading expert in carbohydrate biology (glycoscience), ABL leverages its core expertise in exploiting carbohydrate-protein interactions—essential for pathogens to bind to surfaces and hosts—to develop cutting-edge Pathogen Capture Technology (PCT) for decontamination. Committed to sustainability, ABL focuses on creating environmentally friendly solutions that are both effective and sustainable.
ABL secured support from the European Defence Agency and the European Union’s H2020 programs to develop the decontamination technology aimed at combating biothreats and infectious agents. entityDescription:

The Institute is comprised of three chairs: Chair of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing, Chair of Geoinformation and Chair of Cartography.

The Chair of Geoinformation focuses on teaching courses related to the handling and management of geoinformation, with a particular emphasis on cartography and Geographic Information Systems (GIS). In 2013, the Chair established Croatia’s first Open Source Geospatial Lab (OSGL), which is part of the global GeoForAll network. The lab's mission is to connect academia, industry, and public administration in the use and development of open-source geoinformation systems and data.

In addition to its educational activities, the Chair conducts scientific research in areas such as open data, service-oriented cartography, and GIS.

entityDescription: Igence Radar Ltd was founded in 1995 to develop and exploit models of all aspects of radar operation and performance. The team has many years of experience of radar research and technology leading to an understanding of the scientific principles of EM scattering, radar signal & clutter fluctuations and processing, which underpin the operation of modern radar systems. Radar signal processing algorithms and concepts, developed for the detection of small targets in clutter, have been widely implemented in both experimental and operational radars. We have also considerable experience of tracking including the development and implementation of novel tracking algorithms and the production of mathematical models characterising their performance. We have a solid track record of rapidly prototyping radar software applications to analyse trials data to assess radar performance and to de-risk upgrades to radar signal processing. This capability is built on our Virtual Radar Library (ViRad), which is a library of tried and tested C++ classes for radar simulation, signal processing and performance modelling. It allows us to construct a wide range of reliable, bespoke, radar applications in a timely and cost effective manner. In addition to our work on radar our areas of expertise include: Radar Signal processing (including Maritime Surveillance, Synthetic Aperture, Pulsed-Doppler); Radar project support; Radar modelling, performance prediction and simulation; Bayesian techniques including Bayes Nets and Tracking algorithms; Mathematical modelling; Image exploitation, classification and automatic target recognition; Synthetic Aperture Radar image formation, motion compensation and autofocus; Electromagnetic Scattering e.g. propagation modelling, integral equation description of low grazing angle scattering of microwaves; Change detection (coherent and incoherent SAR change detection, optical change detection); Rapid prototyping of software applications.
